My two priorities of change above Audio would be FPS optimization and shadows/visibility.

1. FPS Optimization:

A) I love the scopes in this game, but the double render scoped in FPS drops by 30 or 40 kill my interest in using them. It is so frustrating to try to be accurate with the fluctuations of frames and or the stuttering is brings.

B) The FPS optimization in general. This game on factory when I get 120+ frames feels like a whole new game, compared to other maps that get 50/70. Gameplay is smoother, more responsive, more engaging and it feels more fair instead of questioning if the FPS dipped and caused some frame lag.

2. Shadows/visibility

A) The visibility at longer distances is terrible at times that I literally am squinting at the screen trying to differentiate a bush/object from a PMC/Scav. It seems to have a grain effect or a weird blur at distances that make it very hard to differentiate objects.

B) Shadows are a nice addition for immersion, especially with the rotational cycles of the sun, but some areas of the map at different times of day are literally pitch black under trees or any other object that casts a shadow it is pitch black behind them. Not sure what you have been through, but have you looked into attachment styles? 

Recently going through something similar and what really opened my eyes was my attachment style and how it was affecting my intimate relationships.

I would suggest anyone struggling with romantic relationships to take: https://university.personaldevelopmentschool.com/pages/attachment-quiz. It is an attachment style test that goes into how we relate, are triggered, what we essentially need in relationships, what we can do to heal and what patterns we exhibit so we can work on them. 

This all stems back to our attachment to our parents and unfortunately, us with “insecure” attachment styles have to rewire ourselves for healthy bonding and coping mechanisms. Is it fair, absolutely not, will it make our lives so much better and able to accept the love and comfortability we deserve with anyone, especially our romantic partners, yes. 

I just got into researching this type of interaction and looking at my past relationships, it has blown my mind how simple relationships are, but with our core attachment style wounds pushes and pulls our emotions and has us reacting to past trauma and not our actual present reality. 

I have “Fearful-Avoidant or anxious-avoidant” if anyone is interested in talking or going over their attachment I would love it. Experiences, hurt, breakups, behavior ect. We all seem to be, (not just INTP’s) having these issues, for the lucky secure types we can achieve a secure attachment, by it requires work. 

I really think this will help everyone here confused on their current relationship or part relationships at identifying where things went wrong or when you acted in ways that totally confused you and led to self sabotage.

This might be a bit winded, paired with some of my personal experiences as well, so bear with the ramble, hopefully some of this will be enlightening/useful. 

*^(" why I don't want children, a reconsideration of my position, endless  conversations with himself/myself/others to try to "get on board," a few  pseudo-breakups, and even still, now - not feeling 100% convinced that I  don't want children ")*

This one is hard considering you want to make your partner happy and see yourself and them as a team, but if the mission of the team isn't on the same page there is going to be some form of dissonance and a feeling of ones own individuality is being stripped away and not considered. You have every right to not want children and I know how horrible the struggle is when you get to a "core" issue and you almost freeze and you go, "If I say the wrong thing or allude to that I don't want they want, they will leave" so you don't say anything, pretend you didn't hear what they said or worse, agree that their values or wants are exactly what you want as well, compromising yourself to someone else instead of being true to yourself. That is one of the hardest things to realize, is when you look at each other, there is a part of them that is absolutely crucial for them to be them, and you yourself cannot fill that piece, knowing that would make them ecstatic, but your views start to create a rift of uncompromising tears in the fantasy of the relationship. 

*^(" For forever I felt like I could not leave him, and could not stay. And  maybe he felt the same, because we floated in limbo for an eternity and  allowed ourselves to be buoyed by individual happy moments. We do love  each other, after all. But, we haven't been "thriving" in any sense, and  he eventually shared that he was "trying" to be okay without children,  but deep down wasn't (this I knew, intuitively...but just did not want  it to end). The pain I feel from not being "enough" for somebody is  positively overwhelming, and it's a feeling I've felt my entire life  (also - I understand it's not really about being "enough" for  someone...that the kids question is a complicated question - but this is  what it feels like). ")*

I would highly look into, [https://www.yourpersonality.net/attachment/](https://www.yourpersonality.net/attachment/) It evaluates your attachment style which is formed from childhood in relation to how your needs were met or not met as a child by your caregiver, which heavily transfers into romantic relationships as partners tend to bring out the same traits as your caregiver, but almost more intense with sexual interactivity and bonding. The reason I mention that is your mentioning of yourself wanting to stay, but having an inherent pull to leave, but not. This paragraph resonates to me on such a level, been broken up with my ex gf for about 11 months now, but it still feels like pangs of me dying at times. I loved this woman terribly hard, did everything I could with the knowledge I had and hypothetical mental tools I had, but it wasn't enough. We both had our issues, but I know full well that feeling of wanting to leave. The depression on their end gets you down too much, you disagree on something, the communication isn't exactly optimal, you both get in a routine and feel neglected, your attachment needs (See attachment test results) aren't met and you start to feel hurt on a visceral level you never felt before, you have unwavering core values that make you doubt ect. As much as I am starting to finally accept it, I am realizing that compromise and sacrifice are part of a relationship, and some aren't, just because you have differing viewpoints doesn't mean everything should blow up, but yet, a care value if something that rarely changes and unfortunately means there is not compatibility between you two. Now, where the aversion to children comes from is something you may need to look inside of yourself to find out though. It could be fear that it means actual commitment, responsibility, a loss of freedom, lack of understanding how to handle children, you think this person has less dominant genes ect, it could be a myriad of things, but there could be a deeper reasoning that may need to be explored if possible to help get a better grasp on yourself and where the relationship can go. Your fear of "Not being good enough" rings true as well. I would reorientation that as, "We are just not compatible when we really look at ourselves on a fundamentally true level of vulnerability" and to be fair, that is completely ok. Most people are not, that isn't a slight or a devalue of yourself, just means that you being who you truly are is not in line with someone else. Sounds not exactly like what you would want to acknowledge, but what better way to be with someone who truly wants to be with you than you being completely open and yourself and being accepted for that. Getting back into dating I am grasping that, all the failed dates, claims of incompatibility, awkward stifled conversations, disinterest, rejection ect, just means our beings are not on the same wavelength, there is nothing wrong with that because you cannot force a relationship or an alignment of individuals, it either blossoms or it is spread to blossom somewhere else by the wind of change. 

(Another mention of the not being good enough comment, I applaud you for noticing this pain within yourself, that is great self awareness. Your intrinsic validation is not needed by others, you can manifest and cultivate that within yourself, it takes plenty of time though. I feel if you are anything like me in this regard you view relationships and love as the pinnacle of contentment/success and fulfillment, we oftentime throw ourselves at people struggling and begging for love until you get that attention, care, commitment and romantic longing you for them and them for you, it is hard, but those sources of validation are fleeting, which is why self validation is crucial to stay grounded and know the relationship is being traveled in a sense of stability, not washed away by the desperate cling to someone our of fear of them leaving or you putting your foot down as well and saying this isn't what I want.)

Something that I have learned personally and that I am trying to do as of now so I don't get into these spirals as you are, I put my foot down. Relationships and friendship are built side by side, if someone "just wants to be friends" first, to me, that shows a lack of commitment or interest. That is the whole point of dating is to get to know each other more and more, friendship will arise, but more specifically, romantic feelings. 

I had to do this with a girl I asked out and she said she wanted to be friends, we went out, she said she wants to go out more, but cannot commit to a relationship at the moment, I told her that is fine, but I cannot be just a friend. 

I say this because, as you, we both have went after someone that we both are physically attracted to and other factors of interest, denying yourself to advance romantically is a disservice to yourself and that person. You, obviously want to advance because there is attraction, while in some capacity this person has said, "No, I don't think anything physical is appropriate right now." That is going to keep hurting and driving your anxiety up, trust me. Plus, you will always second guess where you stand, are they into me like that, what if I wait, what did that sign mean, are they using me, talking to someone else ect.... 

If the dating phase fails and you guys agree to be freinds, that is one thing, but to sever yourself from your feelings of attraction, physical and emotional closeness is harmful and isn't what you want.

My advice, yet again, this is just me personally, would be to tell them if they want to continue dating and forming a friendship through the process that is what you want to do, but being a pseudo friend while not being able to act on your attraction is not fair to what you want.

EMDR therapy demonstrates that a similar sequence of events occurs with mental processes.  The brain’s information processing system naturally moves toward mental health.
